Commercial window treatments in Los Angeles

Daylight should work for the people using your space. We help Los Angeles offices, restaurants and businesses choose interior blinds and shades for screen glare, privacy and the look of the room, with measuring, installation and compatible motorized controls.

Discuss your space(818) 884-5464

Plan around the way your business uses the room.

The windows nearest a workstation may need different coverage from those beside a café table or reception desk. We start by asking where the light becomes a problem, when it happens and what you want people to be able to see.

Offices and meeting rooms

Desk positions, computer screens and meeting spaces all affect the choice. We can discuss how much daylight to keep, where glare is distracting and which windows need more privacy.

Restaurants and cafés

Consider the tables closest to the glass and how the sun moves during service. A treatment should address the light at those tables while fitting the atmosphere you want customers to enjoy.

Shops and street-facing spaces

A storefront view and a private workspace can have different needs. Tell us where visibility is welcome and where people need more coverage, so we can compare the options window by window.

Compare the view, coverage and finish together.

Solar screen shades can reduce glare while keeping a daytime view outside. A lit room may be visible from outside after dark, even when the shades are down.

Tell us when you need privacy and how much daylight you’d like to keep. We can compare more opaque roller fabrics or an additional layer where a screen shade alone won’t give enough coverage.

We can compare colors and textures with your flooring, walls and furnishings so the shades fit the room.

Explore shadesCompare blindsMotorized shade options

Bring the product and installation details together.

Measuring and fit.

Window dimensions are part of the picture. We also consider mounting depth, surrounding trim and the room needed for the treatment to move. These details help shape the product choice and installation plan.

Controls people can use.

Think about who adjusts the shades and how often. We can discuss manual operation and compatible motorized controls for individual shades or groups, including the setup and power requirements of the chosen system.

Scope, budget and timing.

A few office windows and a restaurant with several banks of glass involve different work. Tell us about your priorities, budget and any dates you’re working toward. We’ll discuss product availability and installation arrangements for your project.

John’s commercial work.

John has supplied mesh solar shades for Western Bagel stores in the Valley, where the aim was to cut glare while keeping a view through the windows. His commercial experience also includes window covering work for The Izaka-ya by Katsu-ya.

Questions about commercial blinds and shades

Ask John: (818) 884-5464
Can you help with a small office or just a few windows?

Yes. You don’t need a whole-building project to start a conversation. Tell us about the room, the number of windows and what you want to improve, and we’ll discuss suitable options.

Can I reduce glare and still see outside?

Solar screen shades can reduce glare while keeping a daytime view outside. We’ll help you compare fabrics for the view and level of glare control you want. They may still leave a lit room visible from outside after dark.

Can commercial shades be motorized?

Compatible products can use motorized controls. We can discuss individual shades or groups, control and hub setup, and any power requirements. The available options depend on the treatment and system you choose.

Do you handle measuring and installation?

We handle the measuring and installation, including the mounting details. If you choose motorized shades, we set up the compatible controls as well.

Can you come to my home or business?

You can schedule a consultation for a commercial or residential space. We’ll meet you there, look at the windows and talk through what you have in mind. Photos are welcome if you’d like to send them ahead of the visit.

Tell us what the windows need to do.

Schedule a consultation at your business, and we’ll look at the windows and talk through the options with you. You can also call John to discuss your project or arrange an appointment at our Woodland Hills showroom.
